desktop.usage: MeshBasicMaterial({map, transparent:true, depthWrite:false}); colour is already lit (albedo x light baked); replaces the engine graffiti overlay for that layout

mobile.usage: MeshBasicMaterial({map, transparent:true, depthWrite:false}); colour is already lit (albedo x light baked); replaces the engine graffiti overlay for that layout

units: metres, three.js axes (+Y up); nodes already in engine space (no transform needed)
toneMapping: NeutralToneMapping, exposure 1.0, outputColorSpace SRGB (beauty ref: Blender 'Khronos PBR Neutral')
lightmapUsage: tex.colorSpace=SRGBColorSpace; tex.channel=1; tex.flipY=false; mat.lightMap=tex; mat.lightMapIntensity=entry.lightMapIntensity (= scale*PI because three divides diffuse by PI)
envUsage: HDRLoader env.hdr -> PMREMGenerator.fromEquirectangular, rotation.y = PI/2; give it to metals/floor as material.envMap (envMapIntensity ~0.55 = Blender world strength; v2 env.hdr is desaturated to 15 % and warmed slightly so chrome reads neutral, not blue). Do NOT use scene.environment for the wall: its diffuse light is fully in the lightmap (Blender world only lit glossy rays)

layout.brackets: two wall brackets at x = +-1.62 (part of the Rail mesh)
layout.lights: 5 baked spots at y 4.3 over the rail (x 0, +-1.0, +-1.82; power 1 / 0.8 / 0.62) aimed at the wall at y 1.1, plus a weak frontal fill
